This means you can't accidentally click the OneTab toolbar icon, since you will be presented with a popup window asking you what specifically you'd like to do. Tabs should also restore perfectly - if this isn't the case, please email us and we will reply.

reviews.text: Poped up a update reminder to v2, I clicked yes. Then lost last 5 months tabs. Serious?
reviews.dev_reply:
Hi, what happened is that the v2 storage area (indexeddb) database was suddenly missing. Something external wiped it clean. 

We've had reports that "privacy cleaner" software such as BleachBit and Advanced System Cleaner will try to wipe clean Chrome data stores to destroy your browsing history, and at the same time it wipes OneTab's v2 database.

The reason you saw the popup was that OneTab automatically detected that something external had wiped your v2 database, and gave you the ability to recover old data from a different data store where OneTab v1 data was previously stored.

reviews.text:
What the hell is going on in the July 1st, 2026 update? All my saved tabs have vanished and cannot be recovered. I spent the whole day trying to save them, but there's no viable solution. Everything is like a blank slate. It's insane, and there was no warning! 
I'm going back to using the browser's default bookmarks; it's better. Everything and everywhere all at once sync. This thing will never be on my browser.
reviews.dev_reply:
Hi, today's update was a maintenance update with more features (including better keyboard navigation and the ability expand/collapse groups). 

I'm sorry you lost your data - data loss like this is rare. The upcoming automatic sync feature will make data loss impossible.

What happened to you definitely isn't due to a bug in OneTab. The most likely cause is a disk corruption, which caused Chrome to panic during the regular update. OneTab never writes anything to disk directly - instead extensions ask Chrome to store data, and we have to rely on your browser installation not becoming corrupted due to a disk error, faulty memory chip, or other external interference such as "privacy cleaner" software which can inadvertently corrupt or wipe clean important browser data stores.

Hi [name], OneTab v2 was designed so that unless you dive into the menus, OneTab has an interface that is actually simpler than the old version.

The Chrome Web Store does not make it possible to switch between versions, and that would be a maintenance nightmare anyway, so our focus is on making OneTab v2 as great as possible.

There may be some specific ways we can improve - if so, please email us at one-tab.com/feedback so we know what specifically we should look at working on more.

reviews.text: Bizzarly this plugin forbids you to google anything that starts with "11" and you can't turn that hotkey off. What an intrusive and frustrating design.
reviews.dev_reply:
The "11" shortcut in the browser search bar is to let you search and launch your OneTab bookmarks from any browser window, without having to navigate to the OneTab tab.

If you need to do a regular search query that starts with "11", start typing "11", then after you press space and it indicates a OneTab search is about to happen, you can just press backspace and the browser address bar will act like a normal search bar.

It's unfortunately a limitation of Chrome that Chrome does not let an extension give users the option to disable or change the shortcut.

reviews.text:
Fortunately, I had a backup of an old version. I removed the current version and installed "OneTab 1.86_0" using the "Load unpacked", and everything seems to be working perfectly now.

A major update that completely changes the experience of the extension should not be rolled out in this way, and forced on people who don't want it. At the very least, make the old version available alongside with the new one, and give people the choice to switch back to the old version if they don't like the new update.

For example, I use another extension called "The Marvellous Suspender" to suspend inactive tabs. The old version of OneTab worked seamlessly with this extension, but the new version doesn't even detect the suspended tabs, which makes it tedious to add them one by one after unsuspending them all, and it ruins the easy experience I had with the old version of OneTab.

While some of the new features that were added in the major update are surely wonderful, their addition shouldn't disrupt the seamless workflow of the old version.
reviews.dev_reply: Hi, you're right, we are working right now on matching the experience of the old OneTab much more closely, including the 1-click operation of the OneTab icon. This will include ensuring it is compatible with your other extension. Please contact us at one-tab.com/feedback if you have any other specific issues to report.

reviews.text:
I appreciate the effort to update OneTab, but the new version just doesn’t work well for me.
Side Space does a much better job.
I use Super Session Manager instead of this which is better and serves my purpose perfectly. This is also a good extension nevertheless

- Catastrophic Main Thread Blocking on Chromium browsers (especially on Vivaldi browser) - 

This extension hooks into chrome.tabs.onUpdated way too aggressively without any proper throttling or debouncing. When interacting with heavy SPA sites like YouTube, OneTab completely chokes the event loop to scrape metadata. This introduces severe overhead (easily 100ms+ per state change) and causes 2-3 seconds of total browser UI freeze on browsers with JS-based interfaces like Vivaldi browser. Being on Manifest V3 doesn't excuse lazy event handling. Please fix your background script logic and implement proper debouncing before touching the DOM.
reviews.dev_reply: Hi [name], please could you contact us at one-tab.com/feedback so we can diagnose this issue. We don't ever touch the web page DOM, in fact OneTab doesn't even have permission to do that. Hopefully you can help us reproduce the problem on our end.

reviews.dev_reply:
Thanks for the review, [name]. 

For those that are not aware, if you go to OneTab options and choose "Show the OneTab action popup" option, then clicking the OneTab icon will show a popup window instead of immediately sending tabs to OneTab.

Vivaldi's tab stacks feature is something they don't have an API for - which means OneTab has no way of knowing if tabs are in a stack. If this changes, we will support stacks.
